items.q: An annular itchy plaque with an active scaly edge and central clearing on the trunk is?
items.exp: Tinea corporis is ringworm of glabrous skin with advancing papulovesicular borders, confirmed by KOH showing hyphae.
r: Incorrect. That has target lesions acrally.
Correct. Active edge with central clearing.
Incorrect. That has a herald patch then collarette scale.
Incorrect. That has non-scaly dermal papules.
items.kp: Ring with active edge is tinea corporis.

items.q: A schoolchild has patchy hair loss with black dots and easily pluckable hairs. The likely pattern and test are?
o: Black-dot tinea capitis confirmed by KOH of stubs
Alopecia areata confirmed by pull test
Seborrhoeic dermatitis confirmed by scale culture
items.exp: Black-dot tinea capitis is endothrix infection breaking hairs at the scalp surface; KOH of stubs shows spores.
r: Correct. Black dots are broken infected shafts.
Incorrect. That shows exclamation-mark hairs.
Incorrect. That shows broken hairs of varying length.
Incorrect. That gives greasy scale without hair dots.
items.kp: Black dots in a child mean tinea capitis.

items.q: A painful boggy crusted scalp swelling with pus discharging from follicles and occipital nodes in a boy is?
items.exp: Kerion is a severe inflammatory zoophilic tinea capitis with boggy tender plaque, suppuration and lymphadenopathy.
r: Incorrect. Carbuncles favour the nape in adults.
Incorrect. That gives sinus tracts in adult males.
Incorrect. That gives scarring tufted hairs.
Correct. Boggy scalp plaque with nodes.
items.kp: Boggy scalp with nodes is kerion.

items.q: A farmer has adherent yellow cup-shaped crusts with a mousy odour on the scalp and cicatricial loss. This favus is caused by?
items.exp: Favus shows scutula around hairs with mousy odour and scarring, classically from Trichophyton schoenleinii.
r: Incorrect. That gives body and nail disease.
Incorrect. That spares hair shafts.
Correct. Scutula with odour is favus.
Incorrect. That gives grey-patch tinea.
items.kp: Yellow cups with odour mean favus.

items.q: Itchy soggy scaling between the toes with fissures in a hostel student is most likely?
items.exp: Interdigital tinea pedis gives macerated scaling toe webs from dermatophytes thriving in moist occluded spaces.
r: Incorrect. That gives tapioca vesicles.
Correct. Soggy toe-web scaling.
Incorrect. That gives pits with odour.
Incorrect. That gives well-defined plaques.
items.kp: Soggy toe webs mean tinea pedis.

items.q: Thick yellow nail with subungual debris starting at the free edge and spreading proximally is?
items.exp: Distal lateral disease is the commonest onychomycosis pattern with onycholysis and heaped subungual keratin.
r: Correct. Free-edge spread with debris.
Incorrect. That shows pitting and oil drops.
Incorrect. That shows thinning with pterygium.
Incorrect. That swells the nail folds.
items.kp: Free-edge yellow nail debris is onychomycosis.

items.q: Hypopigmented finely scaling macules on the upper trunk that fluoresce pale yellow under Wood lamp are?
items.exp: Versicolor is Malassezia overgrowth with spaghetti-and-meatball yeast on KOH and yellow fluorescence.
r: Incorrect. That is non-scaly with blue-white glow.
Incorrect. That is faint dry facial patches in children.
Incorrect. That has an active raised border.
Correct. Scaly pale trunk macules with yellow glow.
items.kp: Scaly pale trunk patches mean versicolor.

items.q: A diabetic has beefy-red moist plaques with satellite pustules in the groin folds. The likely agent and mount finding are?
o: Candida with pseudohyphae and budding yeast
items.exp: Cutaneous candidiasis favours moist folds with satellite pustules; KOH shows pseudohyphae with budding yeast.
r: Incorrect. That gives coral-red fluorescence.
Incorrect. That gives grouped vesicles.
Correct. Satellite pustules with pseudohyphae.
Incorrect. That spares folds and lacks satellites.
items.kp: Satellite pustules in folds mean candida.

items.q: A barefoot farmer has a swollen foot with multiple draining sinuses discharging dark grains. The diagnostic triad indicates?
items.exp: Mycetoma triad is painless tumefaction, sinuses and grains, from fungi or actinomycetes after thorn pricks.
r: Incorrect. That shows verrucous plaques with sclerotic bodies.
Correct. Swelling plus sinuses plus grains.
Incorrect. That favours cervicofacial sulphur granules.
Incorrect. That discharges white grains without triad.

items.q: A rose gardener develops a nodule at a prick site followed by similar nodules marching up the forearm. This sporotrichoid spread suggests?
items.exp: Sporotrichosis follows lymphatics with chains of nodules after plant trauma; Sporothrix is dimorphic with cigar bodies.
r: Correct. Nodules marching along lymphatics.
Incorrect. That gives lupus vulgaris plaques.
Incorrect. These give single plaques or ulcers.
Incorrect. That favours mycetoma-like foot disease.
